component: codex plugin v1.0.6 (/home/eranr/.claude/plugins/cache/openai-codex/codex/1.0.6) — cross-model second-opinion harness: delegates review, rescue/fix tasks, adversarial review, and an optional stop-time review gate to the local OpenAI Codex CLI via a per-session app-server broker, a per-workspace job ledger, and strict verbatim-relay contracts

skills.name: /codex:review (commands/review.md)
skills.purpose: Run a native Codex code review of local git state (working tree or branch vs base).
skills.mechanism: Sizes the diff with git shortstat first, asks exactly one wait-vs-background question with the recommended option labeled first, runs codex-companion.mjs review, and returns Codex stdout verbatim under a hard review-only gate (no fixes, no paraphrase).

skills.name: /codex:adversarial-review (commands/adversarial-review.md + prompts/adversarial-review.md)
skills.purpose: Run a Codex review that challenges the approach, design choices, tradeoffs, and assumptions rather than just defects.
skills.mechanism: Same sizing/wait-vs-background flow as review but injects an adversarial prompt template (skeptical operating_stance, attack_surface checklist, 4-part finding_bar, calibration rules favoring one strong finding, JSON schema output with severity/confidence/line ranges) and accepts user focus text; output relayed verbatim, review-only.

skills.name: /codex:rescue (commands/rescue.md)
skills.purpose: Delegate investigation, explicit fixes, or follow-up work to the Codex rescue subagent.
skills.mechanism: Runs inline so the Agent tool stays in scope, checks task-resume-candidate and asks once whether to continue the existing Codex thread or start fresh (skipped when --resume/--fresh given), forwards the raw request to the codex-rescue subagent, and must return Codex output verbatim.
skills.invocation: model-invocable command (also user-typed); warns against Skill(codex:rescue) which re-enters and hangs

skills.name: codex-rescue agent (agents/codex-rescue.md)
skills.purpose: Thin forwarding wrapper that hands a substantial debugging/implementation task to Codex through the shared runtime.
skills.mechanism: Exactly one Bash call to codex-companion task; may only use gpt-5-4-prompting to tighten the forwarded prompt; forbidden from reading the repo, polling, summarizing, or substituting its own answer; defaults to write-capable (--write), maps --resume to --resume-last, returns stdout as-is and returns nothing on failure.
skills.invocation: proactive model-invoked (description says use when Claude is stuck) or via /codex:rescue Agent call

skills.name: /codex:status (commands/status.md)
skills.purpose: Show active and recent Codex jobs for this repository including review-gate status.
skills.mechanism: Reads the per-workspace job ledger; renders a compact single Markdown table for the session list, or full unsummarized output when a job ID is given; supports --wait/--timeout-ms.

skills.name: /codex:result (commands/result.md)
skills.purpose: Show the stored final output of a finished Codex job.
skills.mechanism: Prints the persisted job payload with an explicit no-summarize rule preserving verdict, findings, file paths, line numbers, errors, and follow-up commands exactly.

skills.name: /codex:cancel (commands/cancel.md)
skills.purpose: Cancel an active background Codex job in this repository.
skills.mechanism: Single companion-script call that terminates the tracked job's process tree via the ledger.

skills.name: /codex:transfer (commands/transfer.md)
skills.purpose: Transfer the current Claude Code session into a resumable Codex thread.
skills.mechanism: Imports the Claude JSONL transcript (path from env or --source, validated to live under ~/.claude/projects) into a Codex thread and preserves the codex resume <session-id> command verbatim for the user.

skills.name: /codex:setup (commands/setup.md)
skills.purpose: Check whether the local Codex CLI is installed/authenticated and optionally toggle the stop-time review gate.
skills.mechanism: Runs setup --json, offers install via a single AskUserQuestion (install option first, marked Recommended) only when Codex is missing and npm exists, and flips the stopReviewGate flag in per-workspace state.json.

skills.name: codex-cli-runtime skill (skills/codex-cli-runtime/SKILL.md)
skills.purpose: Internal helper contract governing how the rescue subagent calls the codex-companion runtime.
skills.mechanism: Restricts the subagent to exactly one task invocation, defines flag normalization (spark→model id, --resume→--resume-last, strip execution flags from task text), forbids other subcommands and any repo inspection, and mandates verbatim stdout return with return-nothing-on-failure.
skills.invocation: user-invocable: false; loaded only inside codex-rescue

skills.name: codex-result-handling skill (skills/codex-result-handling/SKILL.md)
skills.purpose: Internal presentation contract for relaying Codex output to the user.
skills.mechanism: Requires preserving verdict/summary/findings/next-steps structure, severity ordering, exact paths/lines, and fact-vs-inference evidence boundaries; a CRITICAL hard stop forbids auto-applying review fixes until the user chooses; failed runs surface stderr and never get a Claude-substituted answer.
skills.invocation: user-invocable: false; auto-applied when handling helper output

skills.name: gpt-5-4-prompting skill (skills/gpt-5-4-prompting/SKILL.md + 3 references)
skills.purpose: Guide for composing Codex/GPT-5.4 prompts as operator-style block-structured contracts.
skills.mechanism: A library of named XML blocks (task, structured/compact output contracts, default_follow_through_policy, completeness_contract, verification_loop, grounding/citation rules, action_safety, research_mode, dig_deeper_nudge) plus end-to-end recipes (diagnosis, narrow fix, review, research, prompt-patching) and an antipatterns file; core rule is tighten the contract before raising reasoning effort.
skills.invocation: user-invocable: false; used by codex-rescue to shape forwarded prompts

skills.name: stop-review-gate (hooks.json Stop + scripts/stop-review-gate-hook.mjs + prompts/stop-review-gate.md)
skills.purpose: Optional gate that has Codex adjudicate whether Claude's last turn may end the session.
skills.mechanism: On Stop, if stopReviewGate is enabled and Codex is available, spawns a Codex task on the previous turn with a strict first-line ALLOW:/BLOCK: output protocol; BLOCK (or timeout/parse failure — the gate fails closed) emits decision:block with a reason, forcing more fixes before stopping; only turns that actually made code edits count.
skills.invocation: hook, off by default; toggled via /codex:setup --enable-review-gate

skills.name: session lifecycle hooks (hooks.json SessionStart/SessionEnd + scripts/session-lifecycle-hook.mjs)
skills.purpose: Manage the shared Codex app-server broker and per-session job hygiene.
skills.mechanism: SessionStart exports session/transcript/broker env vars into CLAUDE_ENV_FILE; SessionEnd shuts down the broker, terminates still-running job process trees for the session, and prunes them from the state ledger.

patterns: Verbatim-relay contract: the delegating agent is a thin forwarder explicitly forbidden from paraphrasing, summarizing, or substituting its own answer, keeping the second opinion genuinely independent of the host model
Reviewer/editor separation as a hard gate: review commands are review-only and the result-handling skill forces a full stop after findings until the user explicitly selects what to fix

Stop-time adjudication gate: an opt-in hook where a second model must answer a machine-parseable first-line ALLOW/BLOCK verdict on the last turn before the session may end, failing closed with a documented manual bypass

Per-workspace job ledger with status/result/cancel verbs: background delegated work is tracked as durable jobs (id, kind, status, phase, stored final payload) surviving across turns, with session-scoped cleanup at SessionEnd
Cost triage before delegation: measure the work size first (diff shortstat), then ask exactly one wait-vs-background question with the recommended option listed first and suffixed (Recommended)

Continue-vs-fresh thread routing: a resume-candidate probe plus one explicit question, with --resume/--fresh flags as consent shortcuts that suppress the question, and delta-only instructions on resumed threads

Composable prompt-block library: named reusable contract blocks (grounding, verification loop, follow-through defaults, dig-deeper nudge) with recipes and an antipatterns file, and the rule 'tighten the contract before raising reasoning effort'

Schema-constrained review output: JSON schema enum verdict plus findings requiring severity, location, confidence 0-1, and a concrete recommendation, with calibration rules preferring one strong finding over filler
Evidence-boundary preservation through relays: fact vs inference vs open-question labels must survive every hand-off unchanged
Fail-visible degradation: if the delegate never ran, report the failure with actionable stderr and produce no substitute answer

Layered invocation policy: disable-model-invocation for user-consent-only commands, user-invocable:false for internal contract skills, and proactive-use description text for the one subagent meant to trigger itself
Cross-tool session transfer: export the host transcript into the other system's native resumable-thread format with path validation and a preserved resume command
knowledgeWorkAnalogs: Adversarial second-reader for drafts: a separate 'red-team my argument' command (distinct from a neutral edit pass) sent to a different model with an attack-surface checklist (unsupported claims, missing counterarguments, citation gaps, logical leaps, overgeneralization) and a 4-part finding bar (what fails, why, impact, concrete revision), returning schema'd findings with severity and confidence, relayed verbatim and never auto-applied to the text

Publish gate: before a report/essay/note is marked final, a stop hook sends the draft to a second model that must answer ALLOW/BLOCK with a short reason (e.g., BLOCK: key claim in section 2 has no source), failing closed with a manual bypass

Research rescue delegation: when a literature search or analysis stalls, forward the exact question to a second research agent under a prompt contract (research_mode separating facts/inferences/open questions, citation_rules preferring primary sources) and present its answer unedited as a labeled second opinion

Job ledger for long-running knowledge tasks: background literature reviews, source-verification sweeps, or corpus indexing tracked as jobs with /status, /result, /cancel, and stored final payloads reviewable days later in the vault

Continue-vs-fresh for inquiries: explicitly choose between resuming an ongoing research thread with delta-only instructions and starting a clean-slate investigation to avoid anchoring on earlier conclusions

Prompt-block library for knowledge work: reusable named blocks (citation_rules, steelman_contract, verification_loop against sources, dig_deeper_nudge for second-order implications) plus recipes for summarize/compare/synthesize and an antipatterns file for vague asks
Evidence-boundary discipline in PKM: notes and summaries must preserve markings distinguishing direct quote, paraphrase, inference, and open question through every compression or relay step
Reviewer-never-rewrites rule for feedback on writing: reviewer output lists located findings only; the author (or a separate apply step with explicit consent per finding) makes changes
Session transfer between thinking tools: export a research conversation into another system's resumable form (an Obsidian note with state, or another model's thread) with the resume handle preserved
Size-based triage for delegated reading: estimate corpus/source volume first, then one question — wait for the synthesis now or run it in the background and check the ledger
